notes: CardDemo CBSTM03B, the file-I/O subprogram CBSTM03A CALLs (CBSTM03A is not a case: it needs the report writer's files). One request block, LK-M03B-AREA (DD X(8), OPER X(1), RC X(2), KEY X(25), KEY-LN S9(4), FLDT X(1000)); KEY-LN is spelled as the corpus spells a positive zoned number ('{' = +0, 'I' = +9, as in its data files): GnuCOBOL rewrites an unsigned digit it reads as a length to that form in place, which IBM would not; the item is compared whole -- the file status the program returns in RC and the record it READs INTO FLDT. Each file is driven through OPEN, READ (TRNXFILE / XREFFILE, sequential access) or keyed READ (CUSTFILE / ACCTFILE, random access) and CLOSE; the end of file (10, then 46), a missing record (23), and the file-state errors (READ before OPEN 47, a second OPEN 41, CLOSE of a closed file 42) are calls of their own. TRNXFILE is the first three records of the corpus's dailytran.txt (trnx.txt here) so its end of file is three READs away; the other three files are the corpus's own data.
